decisions.decision: The measured defect, restated from the coordinator's own re-measurement at cc17473 rather than from V2-065's evidence, because it is worse than the escalation said. domain.RequirementStartFraming occurs in exactly TWO non-test lines in the whole repository -- its declaration at internal/domain/model.go:437 and its switch case at model.go:475 -- and in ZERO non-test lines outside internal/domain. Nothing constructs a domain.RequirementCommand with that Kind anywhere but four test files. There are exactly FOUR non-test u.SaveRequirement call sites: internal/application/service.go:845 (Capture, which constructs the aggregate directly at Status captured, service.go:841, and never calls DecideRequirement), service.go:939 (Plan, which appends an Increment id and bumps Version and does NOT touch Status), internal/application/human_input.go:527 (RequestHumanInput -> needs-input) and human_input.go:656 (AnswerHumanInput -> ready). Both of the latter two require a source status the application can never produce. The consequence is not that one edge is missing: the set of Requirement statuses reachable through every application command is the single element {captured}. domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease also has zero non-test callers, so no Requirement can reach completed either. This task adds exactly ONE edge and takes the reachable set to {captured, framing, needs-input, ready} -- the minimum that makes cap-human-input-request's declared success condition observable, and nothing more.
decisions.rationale: The Work Order's numbers have been stale for nine consecutive tasks, so every figure above was read by the coordinator at cc17473 with a fresh grep and is still to be re-measured by the implementer. The full issuance table measured at cc17473: start-framing (from captured) NONE; ready (from framing/waiting/needs-input) AnswerHumanInput; start (from ready/recovering/waiting) NONE; wait (from ready/active/recovering) NONE; needs-input (from framing/active/evaluating) RequestHumanInput; recover (from active/waiting) NONE; evaluate (from active) NONE; pause (from ready/active/waiting/recovering) NONE; cancel (from anything but completed/cancelled) NONE. Six of the nine commands plus the release-bound completion stay unissued after this task, deliberately: the outcome sentence asks for the state that asks a person a question, not for a Requirement lifecycle driver. internal/runner/orchestrator.go:41-58 is the one place that drives a whole journey, and it drives the INCREMENT to completion (Plan, Prepare, Claim, Start, result) while the parent Requirement sits at captured throughout -- so the missing driver is not hidden there either.

decisions.decision: The transition is issued by an explicit, separately-addressed caller command -- Service.StartFraming -- and NOT by Service.Capture advancing on its own, NOT by a flag on CaptureRequest, and NOT by a reconciler or scheduler sweep that walks captured Requirements. A Requirement leaves captured only when a caller names that Requirement and asks for that transition, carrying its own request_id and its own expected version.
decisions.rationale: Judged against non_goals item 2 ('do not let a Requirement leave its captured status without a caller asking for it'), which each rejected option violates in a different way. (a) Advancing inside Capture: the Capture caller asked to record a Requirement, not to start shaping it, so the transition would happen because of a request that did not ask for it; worse, it would make `captured` a status no observer can ever see, turning a declared domain status into an internal instant and leaving the captured->framing edge the domain declares as permanently dead code -- the same class of unreachable-constant drift already recorded as E3 for ReleaseStatus. It would also change CaptureResponse.Version from 1 to 2 and move every capture request fingerprint, breaking existing tests and the openapi response contract for no gain. (b) A boolean like start_framing on CaptureRequest: the caller does ask, but it fuses two transitions into one idempotency key, so a partial retry cannot be reasoned about, and it still erases the observable captured state. (c) A reconcile sweep: no caller asks at all -- the Loop would advance every captured Requirement on a timer, which is precisely the shape non_goals item 2 forbids, and internal/reconciler is prohibited here anyway. The separate command is also the only option under which the M5 dogfood can observe the captured state and then observe it being left, which is what the defect measurement needs to become a repair measurement.

decisions.decision: The command accepts exactly the role pair Capture accepts: RoleOwner and RoleScheduler, via callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner, RoleScheduler). It is NOT scheduler-only and it is NOT runner-callable. The HTTP route gates the same pair, and the owner is the role that must work.
decisions.rationale: The decisive measurement, and it changes the answer. NO non-test code path anywhere in this repository constructs an application.Caller with Role RoleScheduler. Measured at cc17473: the only non-test Caller constructions are internal/api/auth.go:50 and :85 (RoleRunner, from a verified runner session header) and auth.go:59 and :99 (RoleOwner, from the IAP assertion or the preview-local owner bearer token), plus internal/runner/orchestrator.go:39-40, which fabricates an owner caller with subject 'runner-local-owner' precisely because it has no scheduler identity to use. Every RoleScheduler occurrence outside tests is a role ACCEPTED by a command, never a role PRODUCED by a transport. A scheduler-only start-framing command would therefore be unreachable over CombinedAuthenticator (production IAP) and over LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator (preview-local) alike -- an application command whose precondition no real caller can satisfy, which is this task's own defect reproduced one level up. Runner is excluded for the reason V2-065 excluded the owner from asking: a Runner executes an Increment it was handed; it does not decide that a Requirement should start being shaped, and letting it would make the recorded actor unusable as attribution. Accepting the scheduler alongside the owner costs nothing and matches Capture, Plan, Prepare, Control and RegisterRepository, so the pair is the established idiom rather than a new one.

decisions.decision: The command follows Capture's discipline and RequestHumanInput's transition mechanism, in a new file internal/application/framing.go. Capture's half: requireRequest(req.RequestID), requestFingerprint("start-framing", req), s.mutate(ctx, "start-framing:"+req.RequestID, ...), u.Idempotency(ctx, req.RequestID, "start-framing") with a fingerprint-conflict refusal and restoreResponse replay, and a domain.Permit evaluation. RequestHumanInput's half: the status change is domain.DecideRequirement with domain.RequirementCommand{Kind: domain.RequirementStartFraming, Actor: actor, At: transaction authority time, ExpectedVersion: req.ExpectedVersion}, saved with u.SaveRequirement(ctx, next, r.Version), recorded through s.record with event type requirement.framing-started, and staging NO outbox item.
decisions.rationale: The two precedents answer different questions and both are followed. Plan (service.go:882) and Prepare (service.go:986) are the precedent for a canonical-state change with no outbox item, and their idempotency shape is identical to Capture's; what must NOT be copied from them is their absence of a Permit (see d5). Capture (service.go:743) is the precedent for the idempotency-plus-fingerprint-plus-Permit trio on a Requirement-scoped write. RequestHumanInput (human_input.go:460) is the precedent -- and, with AnswerHumanInput, the only precedent -- for driving domain.DecideRequirement from this layer at all: measured, domain.DecideRequirement has exactly three non-test references in internal/application, one of which is a comment (human_input.go:22), so this command is the THIRD real transition issued from the application layer and must not invent a fourth idiom. A new file rather than an addition to service.go for two measured reasons: service.go is 1723 lines and is covered by several other tasks' evidence keys, and V2-065 set the precedent of a task-owned file (human_input.go) for a new command family. The new file must import none of os/exec, net/http, net/url, internal/provider or internal/runner: internal/application/source_guard_test.go parses every *.go file in the package, test files included, and a module-path literal in source text is read by internal/ci's manifest derivation as a declared component edge.

decisions.decision: The Permit kind is domain.PermitClaim, evaluated with domain.Permit ONLY and never passed to domain.EffectFromPermit. The resulting seven-mode behaviour is the design, and it is asserted rather than described: allow ALLOWS, pause-intake ALLOWS, pause-claim DENIES, graceful-stop DENIES, immediate-stop DENIES, emergency-stop DENIES, cancel DENIES. No new PermitKind is introduced.
decisions.rationale: Derived from the measured gate at internal/domain/control.go:266-282, not chosen for convenience. permitAllowed returns, for pause-intake, kind != PermitIntake; for pause-claim, kind != PermitClaim; for graceful-stop, kind == PermitCheckpoint only; and false for immediate-stop, emergency-stop and cancel. Three candidates were judged. (i) Permit-free, copying Plan and Prepare: REJECTED, because it would let a Requirement change canonical status under emergency-stop, and a stop that still permits canonical state to move is not a stop. That Plan and Prepare already have this property is a measured DEFECT of theirs, recorded here for the coordinator as a separate finding and deliberately not propagated -- a precedent is not an argument when the precedent is the thing being escalated elsewhere. (ii) PermitIntake, copying Capture and AnswerHumanInput: REJECTED, because pause-intake means 'take no new work in, finish what you already have', and framing an ALREADY-captured Requirement is finishing what you have; denying it would make pause-intake a full stop by accident. (iii) PermitClaim: ACCEPTED, because starting to shape a Requirement is the first commitment of Loop capacity to it, which is exactly what pause-claim exists to withhold, and because every stop mode denies it. The V2-059 finding cited in the brief -- that anything requiring a durable effect is denied in every pause mode, since EffectFromPermit (control.go:297-303) requires current.Mode == ControlAllow exactly -- is why the decision to stage NO durable effect is load-bearing here: it is what lets pause-intake still allow framing. domain.Permit alone is the correct gate precisely because PermitKind.SideEffect() is false for PermitClaim (control.go:199-201) and nothing external is asked to do anything.

decisions.decision: The ControlTarget is resolved inside the transaction from the Requirement's own Repository link, not from configuration and not from the request: u.RequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, requirementID) supplies RepositoryID when a link exists and an empty RepositoryID when it does not, and domain.EffectiveControl(controls, target) supplies the revision the Permit is checked against. StartFramingRequest carries NO control_revision and NO repository_id field.
decisions.rationale: Two measured constraints force this. ServiceConfig deliberately holds no repository id (service.go's ServiceConfig comment, V2-071 A6 / dp-v2-071 d14) because an Installation registers many Repositories and a per-process id would make a domain.ScopeRepository intent match the wrong Repository; Plan already resolves the link this way inside its own transaction (service.go:947-960 at cc17473) and Capture derives its revision from EffectiveControl rather than from the caller (service.go:816-824). A caller-supplied revision would additionally be a trap: domain.Permit refuses unless request.ControlRevision is EXACTLY control.Revision, so a caller that has not re-read controls would be denied for a reason unrelated to the owner's intent. Deriving the revision internally makes the exactness check trivially true and leaves the mode as the only thing that can deny.

decisions.decision: One new HTTP route: POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:start-framing, added to internal/api/api.go's POST switch default branch by the same prefix-plus-suffix idiom the file already uses for :renew, :start, :request-input and :answer-input, gated to RoleOwner or RoleScheduler, and declared in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml. NO owner-console control is added: internal/web/owner.js and internal/web/owner.html are not touched, and neither is docs/preview/capabilities.md.
decisions.rationale: The route is required, not optional: the surface the M5 dogfood and TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive drive is HTTP, so a command with no route would leave the outcome unobservable exactly as today. The suffix is collision-free by construction and by measurement: the existing /v1/executions/{id}:start branch is prefix-gated on /v1/executions/, and ':start-framing' does not satisfy HasSuffix(path, ':start'); the GET /v1/requirements/ prefix branch is method-gated. The console is excluded on chain grounds and on declaration grounds. cap-human-input-request declares exactly one owner surface, /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}, which is a READ, and the console block V2-065 added already renders the question and submits the answer; a 'start framing' button is part of no declared observable_result, so adding one would enrol this task in the internal/web chain and move the web component key for no declared gain. Chain position, stated for the coordinator: touching openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest, so this task joins the api-contract chain and must be serialized against any task holding contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, internal/api/api.go or internal/application; concretely it conflicts with V2-079 (queued), which holds internal/api/api_test.go, internal/api/live_local_test.go and internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, and must run after it. It stays entirely out of the internal/web and docs chains.

decisions.decision: internal/domain is not edited, at all. The transition, its guard and its status already exist; the whole task is that the application layer issues a command the domain has always accepted. No new RequirementCommandKind, no new RequirementStatus, no new PermitKind, no change to any allowed() list.
decisions.rationale: Measured directly: internal/domain/model.go:475-479 already admits RequirementStartFraming from RequirementCaptured and sets Status to RequirementFraming, and model.go:495-499 already admits RequirementNeedInput from framing/active/evaluating. So the ONLY thing standing between a captured Requirement and the state that asks a question is a call. M1's closure proof (the breadth-first fixpoint over DecideRequirement, internal/domain/model.go:398) covers this aggregate; adding the edge to the application changes no reachable status set inside the domain and cannot invalidate it, whereas any domain edit would have to re-establish it. This is also why the fix is small enough to be honest: a repair that needs no domain change is a repair that cannot have widened the state machine.

decisions.decision: No read model changes. internal/application/readmodels.go is prohibited by design, not by omission. GET /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} already reports the framing status through RequirementDetailView.Status, and nextAction is status-agnostic apart from completed and cancelled, so a framing Requirement with no Increment continues to report 'plan increments' exactly as a captured one does.
decisions.rationale: Measured at readmodels.go:306-329: nextAction branches on completed/cancelled, then on Execution status, then on Increment status, then on whether the Increment list is empty; the framing status enters none of those branches, so the response shape and every existing assertion about it are untouched. RequirementDetailView.Status is already the field the dogfood reads to detect the defect (internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:1032-1035 compares status before and after the refused ask), so the repair is observable through the field the measurement already uses, with no new field and no new key in any response.

decisions.decision: The proof is split by what can actually be executed under this task's authorisations, and each part is labelled with what it does and does not establish. (1) Against the REAL cmd/control-plane binary and the REAL Firestore emulator over real HTTP, TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive is extended to capture a Requirement, POST :start-framing as the owner, and read the detail back showing status framing and version incremented -- executed, because that test needs no Provider. (2) Against the composed api.Handler over real HTTP with the in-memory store, the FULL chain is asserted end to end: capture -> :start-framing -> :request-input as a runner -> GET detail showing the needs_input object with its reason class, options with impacts and both scope lists -> :answer-input as the owner -> same Requirement id, unchanged Requirement count, status ready. (3) The full chain against real everything is NOT executed here and is the M5 re-dogfood's to run.
decisions.rationale: Measured constraint that forces the split: :request-input requires a runner session, and internal/api/live_local_test.go has no runner enrolment -- it composes LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator via AGENTIC_LOOP_LOCAL_OWNER_TOKENS and drives owner-authenticated routes only. Adding runner enrolment to that file would duplicate the dogfood fixture's enrol flow and is out of scope. So the segment that real persistence can prove is exactly the segment this task repairs -- that a Requirement leaves captured -- and that is the honest boundary. Part (2) is a real HTTP surface with a real role gate, and it is the only place the whole declared success condition is asserted in one run. Naming the boundary this way is what non_goals item 3 requires: the capability is not claimed exercised by any part of this.

decisions.decision: The dogfood tripwire is converted from a defect probe into the exercise it was written to become, and the check is recorded SKIPPED. internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go's capHumanInputRequest currently FAILS ON PURPOSE if the ask succeeds; that inverted assertion is replaced by the full drive (capture -> :start-framing -> :request-input -> detail -> :answer-input) with the recorded E22-2 history and its date kept in the comment as history. The check is recorded with status skipped, stating that it was COMPILED and go vet clean but NOT executed because TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood additionally requires AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 and makes real claude invocations this task does not authorise.
decisions.rationale: Direct precedent, same shape, one task earlier: wo-v2-079 A12 did exactly this to capBacklogVisibility. The current helper's own failure message asks for it in so many words -- 'the measured precondition gap below no longer holds and this capability's eligibility must be re-judged, not assumed' -- and V2-082 is the task that supplies the judgement. Measured gate: internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:286-299 skips without AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_DOGFOOD=1 and then FATALS rather than skipping on any missing prerequisite, including the provider gate, so a half-configured run can never be counted as an exercise. Leaving the inverted assertion in place would be worse than either alternative: it would sit in the tree asserting a defect that no longer exists, and the next reader would have to guess whether it is history or a live claim.

decisions.decision: cap-human-input-request becomes DEMONSTRABLE, not demonstrated, and the difference is written into the evidence in those terms. After this task the declared success condition -- the Requirement detail shows the needs-input reason, options, impacts and stop/continue scope, and after the answer the SAME Requirement resumes -- is reachable through the real HTTP surface for the first time. What still does not exist is the automatic decision to ask: V2-065 d13's residual stands unchanged, and nothing in this task routes a policy denial, a budget exhaustion or an unclassifiable failure into needs-input. The M5 re-dogfood is REQUIRED and is a coordinator-owned follow-up; no evidence record from this task may contain the phrase 'capability exercised', and none may cite a capability id.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 3 is explicit, and the failure this task exists to repair was itself a declared observable with nothing behind it -- writing 'exercised' because a route now exists would recreate it at one remove. The reason the M5 re-dogfood is required rather than merely nice: the dogfood's recorded verdict for this capability is FAILED with bucket ESCALATION on the ground that the precondition is unreachable, and that ground becomes false at this commit, so the verdict must be re-issued by the exercise rather than amended by argument. Not citing a capability id keeps internal/contracts' capability-evidence reverse check, which is scoped to V2-022's records, green.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api
risks: The role decision is the single point on which the whole repair rests, and it rests on a negative measurement: that no non-test code produces a RoleScheduler caller. If the implementer finds any transport, composition root or cmd/** wiring that does produce one, d3's reasoning weakens and the finding must be escalated rather than used to narrow the route to scheduler-only. The route must remain owner-callable in every case.

d5 departs from the Plan/Prepare precedent on purpose. If the implementer reads the control gate differently -- for instance concluding that PermitClaim wrongly denies framing under pause-claim -- that is a design disagreement, not an implementation detail: stop and escalate. Do not resolve it by removing the Permit, and do not resolve it by adding a PermitKind, which would require editing internal/domain.

StartFraming increments the Requirement version, so a caller that frames before planning must pass the post-framing version to Plan. Existing callers that skip framing are unaffected because Plan reads the version from the request, but internal/runner/orchestrator.go's journey and every existing test that captures then plans at version 1 must keep passing byte-for-byte; if any of them changes, the command was not additive.

contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is a bundle api-contract role member and the contracts component root, so editing it moves both the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest. That is expected. What must not happen is writing any digest value into a document.

internal/api/api_test.go, internal/api/live_local_test.go and internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go are all held by V2-079, which is queued. Running these two tasks concurrently produces conflicts in three test files. Serialize V2-082 after V2-079.

The one thing this task cannot prove is the thing the capability is judged on. The full chain against a real Provider-gated dogfood is not executed here, so an implementer under pressure to close the loop may be tempted to record the rewritten dogfood helper as passing. It is recorded skipped, and the api evidence record's overall result is partial, never passed.
